parts.text:
5
Forces of magnitudes 2 N, 4 N and 7 N combine to produce a resultant force.
The magnitudes of the three forces are fixed, but the forces may act in any direction in the same
plane.
What is not a possible magnitude of the resultant force?
A
0 N
B
5 N
C
8 N
D
13 N

hints: Notice the $2 \text{ N}$, $4 \text{ N}$ and $7 \text{ N}$ forces can point in any direction, so check the two extreme line-ups with all in one line.
Connect the extremes to addition: maximum is the sum $2+4+7$, minimum is the largest $7 \text{ N}$ minus the sum $2+4 \text{ N}$ acting opposite to it.
Compare each listed $0 \text{ N}$, $5 \text{ N}$, $8 \text{ N}$ and $13 \text{ N}$ value with the continuous range from $1 \text{ N}$ to $13 \text{ N}$ to spot the one outside it.
walkthrough: Find the largest possible resultant by putting all forces in the same direction: $R_{max} = 2 + 4 + 7 = 13 \text{ N}$.

Find the smallest possible resultant by putting the largest force opposite to the other two combined: $R_{min} = 7 - (2 + 4) = 1 \text{ N}$, because $2 \text{ N}$ and $4 \text{ N}$ together cannot fully balance $7 \text{ N}$.
By varying the angles in the plane between these two line-ups, the resultant magnitude can take any value continuously from $1 \text{ N}$ up to $13 \text{ N}$.
The value $0 \text{ N}$ is less than the $1 \text{ N}$ minimum, so it cannot be produced while the other values can. This is option A

A.explanation: The smallest possible resultant is $7 - (2+4) = 1 \text{ N}$, so $0 \text{ N}$ is below the minimum and cannot be formed.

B.explanation: $5 \text{ N}$ lies between the $1 \text{ N}$ minimum and $13 \text{ N}$ maximum and can be obtained by suitable angles between the $2 \text{ N}$, $4 \text{ N}$ and $7 \text{ N}$ forces.

C.explanation: $8 \text{ N}$ lies between the $1 \text{ N}$ minimum and $13 \text{ N}$ maximum and can be obtained by partly aligning the three forces.

D.explanation: $13 \text{ N}$ is the maximum $2+4+7$ obtained when all three forces act in the same direction.
